title: Add explicit provider rate-limit handling for model turns
description:
Problem
Eshyra currently has generic model/provider failure handling: model turn failures roll back the turn savepoint and surface a generic "turn could not be completed" CLI message. That protects state, but rate-limit failures are not classified or explained distinctly. A rate-limited Claude/Anthropic token currently exercises only the generic failed-turn path.

Goal
Add explicit rate-limit classification and user-facing handling for model/provider calls, especially gameplay turns, without weakening rollback behavior or adding retry loops that burn quota.

Scope
- Classify provider/model rate-limit failures in the model adapter/error layer.
- Preserve the existing failed-turn rollback behavior: the player's last input must not be applied if the model call fails.
- Surface a clearer CLI message for rate limits, e.g. "Model provider rate limit reached. Try again later. Your last input was not applied."
- Keep provider details sanitized; do not print secrets or raw credential-bearing process/environment details.
- If the Claude Agent SDK exposes retry-after or structured status metadata, capture it in a safe internal diagnostic and optionally include a human-friendly wait hint.
- Do not implement automatic retries for normal gameplay turns unless bounded and explicitly justified. Avoid retry loops that consume more quota.
- Ensure the generic provider-failure path remains for non-rate-limit errors.

Implementation notes
Likely areas:
- packages/core/src/model/AgentSdkModelClient.ts or adjacent model error types
- packages/core/src/engine/turn.ts / runTurn failure handling
- packages/cli command path that prints failed-turn messages
- tests around fake model clients and CLI output

Acceptance criteria
- A fake/rate-limit-shaped model failure is classified as a rate-limit error.
- Gameplay turn failure due to rate limit rolls back the turn savepoint exactly like other model failures.
- CLI output clearly identifies rate limiting and states that the last input was not applied.
- Non-rate-limit provider failures still use the existing generic failed-turn behavior.
- Tests cover:
  - rate-limit classification from a representative Claude/Agent SDK failure shape;
  - failed-turn rollback with rate-limit error;
  - CLI user-facing message for rate limit;
  - secret sanitization / no credential leakage.
- Existing tests continue to pass.

Manual validation
With a known rate-limited Claude/OAuth/API token, run a fresh campaign and enter a simple player action. Confirm:
- Eshyra does not crash.
- The message says the provider is rate limited or equivalent.
- The failed player input is not persisted/applied.
- The user can quit cleanly.
close_reason: Rate-limit classification, CLI messaging, and session/usage exhaustion coverage all complete. PR #245 open.
